pages.title: HTTP workbench

pages.description: Send bounded HTTP and REST requests locally with methods, headers, auth, bodies, TLS verification, redirect control, timing, response evidence, and cURL export.

status.label: Stable core + current source
status.detail: Stable v0.6.1 includes the HTTP foundation. Environment templates, library import and reviewed cURL import below require matching current source.

flow.title: Write one explicit request
flow.detail: Choose the method, URL, query, headers, auth, body, timeout, and redirect policy.

flow.title: Use the local Go relay
flow.detail: ProtoPeek validates a bounded request and keeps TLS verification on by default.

flow.title: Separate response evidence

pages.title: gRPC workbench

flow.title: Send the native RPC shape
flow.detail: Keep metadata, deadline, TLS choice, payload, stream mode, and cancellation visible.

flow.title: Follow the evidence in order

pages.title: WebSocket and SSE workbench
pages.documentTitle: WebSocket & SSE Client: Live Message Evidence | ProtoPeek
pages.description: Connect to WebSocket or SSE services locally, inspect bounded message timelines, send text or binary WebSocket data, and stop each session explicitly.
pages.question: What is this live service sending?

status.label: Stable · v0.6.1
status.detail: The WebSocket/SSE foundation is available in v0.6.1. Sessions start only with Connect and stop on Disconnect, navigation or their limits.

flow.title: Choose the native protocol
flow.detail: Enter one WebSocket or SSE endpoint, headers and a finite duration. Connect starts traffic.

flow.title: Inspect the message timeline
flow.detail: Read data, encoding, named SSE events, IDs and the negotiated WebSocket subprotocol.

flow.title: End the finite session
flow.detail: Disconnect or leave the workbench to close the upstream connection. SSE does not retry automatically.

flow.title: Treat evidence as bounded
flow.detail: Headers and certificate observations are not a vulnerability score or universal verdict.

currentCapabilities.label: HTTP recipes
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source adds environment templates, session-only secrets, request-library import and reviewed cURL import. Loading prepares an unsent editor.

currentCapabilities.label: gRPC stream evidence
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source renders incremental native messages, headers and completion evidence. Local cancellation retains messages without inventing final server status.

currentCapabilities.label: Cap’n Proto plans
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source implements generic bindings and bounded typed returned-capability call plans. Review and Run are separate actions.

currentCapabilities.label: Network diagnostics
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source implements finite DNS/resolver, TCP/TLS, proxy, protocol and offline subnet checks with explicit Run/Cancel controls.

currentCapabilities.label: Packet payload evidence
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source adds default-off bounded TCP payload reconstruction with directional segments, gaps and conflicting overlaps, plus conservative snapshot comparison and Nmap-to-map previews.

currentCapabilities.label: macOS native evidence
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source implements native unprivileged ICMP and aggregate interface counters with native CI fixtures. Real runtime/intermediate-hop acceptance is separate; socket/process ownership remains unavailable.

currentCapabilities.label: Private access
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source adds a separate Headscale HTTPS login-server flow and native NetBird evidence/actions. Installed tools, accounts, permissions and real-provider acceptance remain explicit prerequisites.

currentCapabilities.label: Reviewed publishing
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source implements guarded canonical-user-config writes and owned temporary publishing on Windows/Linux. Linux requires a direct native vendor Go command. Foreground publishing remains unavailable on macOS; provider/account and cleanup acceptance stay separate.

currentCapabilities.label: Optional extension library
currentCapabilities.summary: Current source provides 20 lazy optional entries with explicit integration levels and per-entry host checks. Six are native workbenches; fourteen are setup guides or links. Opening the library installs, downloads and executes nothing.
